sources.title: When should I use web search, extended thinking, and research?

folds.title: Three ways to dig deeper
points: Picking the right one saves time and usage.

folds.title: Web search
points: The weather, a company, recent news.
Claude looks it up and answers.

folds.title: Extended thinking
points: For complex reasoning that needs no fresh web info.
Like debugging code or improving an algorithm.

folds.title: Research
points: Claude runs several searches that build on each other.
Then it writes an in-depth answer.
It takes longer and can use your limits faster, so save it for jobs that need it.

chat.label: Extended thinking

chat.label: Research
chat.you: Find and sum up what experts say about four-day work weeks.

chat.label: Web search

chat.label: Extended thinking

chat.label: Research

chat.label: Web search

chat.label: Extended thinking
chat.you: Find the bug in this short piece of code.

chat.label: Research
chat.you: Write a report on the ways to charge an electric car in my country.

folds.question: You want a detailed comparison of several phone plans from many sources. What fits best?
folds.why: A broad question across many sources is a research job. Web search suits a quick, factual question.
